purpose: P3-S8 A-07: the runtime grant matrix over the DISCOVERED Phase 3 surface — every relation a database built from 0000 through phase2PrefixEnd does not have, which is Phase 3 and every phase after it. For every runtime principal and PUBLIC: the exact SELECT on each such table (table or column level), no write privilege of any kind, and the exact routines it may EXECUTE.
source: infrastructure/database/migrations/0053_inventory_units_and_product_configuration.sql through 0073_default_warehouse_locale_name.sql (the Phase 3 corrective 0070-0073 included) for the Phase 3 scope; 0074_phase4_registry_widening.sql onwards for the entries beyond it.
note: This file is the INTENDED model. The P3-S8 grant-matrix suite (T-04) compares it against the live PostgreSQL catalogues, in both directions: an entry here that the database does not grant is a broken deployment, and a grant the database holds that is absent here is an unreviewed privilege. That comparison runs over the WHOLE discovered surface, Phase 4's own relations included, because it is a law over whatever exists rather than a claim about what will: a migration that grants SELECT on a new table is red until a reviewer records the grant here, which is exactly the change a reviewer must see. Editing this file does not widen anything; a migration does. The one entry that is an INVENTORY rather than a law is phase3Tables, and it is the inventory of the PHASE 3 SCOPE alone — the relations the accepted, digest-verified files 0053 through phase3ScopeEnd create (P4-AL-88): 0000-0073 is frozen byte for byte, so no later phase can enter that scope, and 'and nothing more' still holds of it. A relation a later phase creates is outside that inventory and inside every law.

excludedFromRuntime.daftar_migrator: the deployment principal, not a runtime credential

forbiddenPrivilegesApplyTo: every runtime principal and PUBLIC, on every Phase 3 table, at table and at column level

executeNotes.daftar_app: The 27 signed entry routines (one per registered operation kind) plus the two INVOKER read functions purchase_ap_outstanding and purchase_settlement_state (0065, replaced in 0067 and, purchase_ap_outstanding, in 0072). S7 adds none; S8 adds none; the Phase 3 corrective 0072 (TD-16) adds purchase_write_off_residue, the routine of its one operation kind. Beyond the Phase 3 scope, 0078 adds sale_commit, the signed entry routine of the sale.commit operation kind, granted to daftar_app and to nobody else — its three helpers (sale_lock_commit_targets, sale_document_number, sale_bridge_commit) carry no EXECUTE grant at all, so the only way into them is the entry routine's own DEFINER body. And 0075 adds the four INVOKER receivables read functions — invoice_outstanding, invoice_settlement_state, customer_ar_outstanding and customer_ar_aging — granted to daftar_app and to daftar_inventory_internal, and to nobody else; PUBLIC holds EXECUTE on none of them.
executeNotes.daftar_platform: The two inventory key-domain routines (L:1868) plus the three provisioning routines 0070 (TD-18) re-created and handed to daftar_provisioning_internal: provision_actor(text[]) and the provisioning key install/retire commands. Each keeps its accepted Phase 1 grant to the platform alone; TD-18 closed the TL-3 exception set (no replaced routine is owned by the applier or pins a public-first path any more).
executeNotes.public: No Phase 3 routine, definer or invoker, is executable by PUBLIC.
executeNotes.beyondPhase3Scope: Entries for relations and routines a later phase creates are reviewed here on the same terms as the Phase 3 ones. They are NOT an allowlist that admits them: they are the reviewed statement of which grants exist, and every law in the suite — the forbidden privileges, the by-USE DML refusal sweep, the definer law — still applies to them in full.

prePhase3TableRuntimePrivileges.note: The table-level runtime privileges on the pre-Phase-3 tables that gained a Phase 3 column: exactly the frozen Phase 1 set (0006:77-78, the defect of L:9), identical at 0052 and at 0069. Every Phase 3 column on them is protected by its named invoker guard.
